bonuses.requirements: Blink Releases Attack Review and Offers Up to 3.3 BTC RewardHomeFeedNewsBlink Releases Attack Review and Offers Up to 3.3 BTC RewardBlink Releases Attack Review and Offers Up to 3.3 BTC Reward10/04 12:30According to monitoring by Bitcoin News, Blink has released a complete review of the attack incident that occurred on September 19: this attack resulted in the theft of a total of 6.61 BTC from 24 customer accounts. The company stated that the vulnerability has existed since October 2023, allowing any user with a free Blink account to gain customer service-level access, take over customer accounts, and increase withdrawal limits. The attackers also obtained partial information from 3,817 accounts, including some phone numbers and email addresses; however, names, identification documents, addresses, passwords, and mnemonic phrases were not leaked. All 24 stolen accounts did not have two-factor authentication enabled. The attackers attempted to make 18 withdrawals from 9 accounts that had two-factor authentication protection, but all attempts were unsuccessful. Blink shareholders have fully compensated all affected customers. Approximately 5 BTC of the stolen funds were subsequently transferred via cross-chain exchange services. UBS Research Report Analysis: S&P 500 P/E Ratio Drops 17%, Fed's Rate Hike Path to Determine Market Outlook | HTX InsightsHomeCrypto NewsАналіз ринкуUBS Research Report Analysis: ...UBS Research Report Analysis: S&P 500 P/E Ratio Drops 17%, Fed's Rate Hike Path to Determine Market OutlookmarsbitPublished on 2026-09-29Last updated on 2026-09-29AbstractUBS Research Report Summary: S&P 500 P/E Down 17%, Fed's Rate Path Key to Market Outlook

A UBS report dated September 28, 2026, highlights that the S&P 500's forward P/E ratio has fallen 17% from its November peak, nearing the 20-30% declines typical of recessions. This drop coincides with a roughly 100-basis-point rise in the 10-year Treasury yield year-to-date, driven by a market shift from pricing rate cuts to pricing further hikes. Historical analysis shows the Federal Reserve's subsequent actions are crucial for equity direction.

The 10-year yield has reached 5.2%, significantly above its one-year moving average. In the past 40 years, it has breached 1.5 standard deviations above this average only seven times. In three instances (1994, 1999, 2022) where the Fed subsequently hiked rates over 100 basis points, the S&P 500 delivered negative or flat returns over the following year. In the other four episodes with mild or no hikes (2013, 2016, 2021, 2023), the index posted positive returns, averaging a 17.7% gain one year later.

Currently, markets price in about 88 bps of hikes over the next year, below the 100-bps threshold, suggesting a more moderate path is likely. Despite the P/E compression, which aligns with the 1994 cycle, UBS's valuation framework indicates the index trades at a ~21% discount to its implied P/E, supported by strong earnings growth and improved fundamentals.
